name: Cellulose
notes: Cellulose-associated hydrolytic and oxidative enzymes; includes endoglucanases, cellobiohydrolases, and LPMOs.

name: Hemicellulose
notes: Includes xylan, mannan, xyloglucan, and galactan-associated enzymes.

name: Pectin
notes: Includes polygalacturonases, pectin/pectate lyases, and enzymes targeting pectin side chains.

name: Other Plant Structural Polymers
notes: Includes arabinogalactan and cutin; cutin is a polyester

name: Storage Polysaccharides
notes: Includes fructan, starch, and glycogen degradation-associated enzymes; glycogen is also found in microbes.

name: Chitin
notes: Includes chitinases and chitin-active oxidative enzymes; chitin occurs in fungal cell walls and arthropod exoskeletons.

name: Bacterial Cell Wall Polymers
notes: Primarily peptidoglycan-associated hydrolases and lytic enzymes, including lysozymes.

name: Mixed/Unassigned Polymers
notes: Genes with mixed or uncertain polymer substrate assignments that do not fit confidently into the other categories.

name: Cellulose-Associated
notes: β-Glucoside processing enzymes; may support utilization of cellulose-derived oligosaccharides but are not cellulose-specific.

name: Hemicellulose-Associated
notes: Genes associated with xylooligosaccharides, xyloglucan-derived oligosaccharides, and mannooligosaccharides.

name: Pectin-Associated
notes: Genes potentially involved in processing pectin-derived oligosaccharides; substrate specificity requires verification.

name: Storage-Associated
notes: Genes associated with fructooligosaccharides and maltooligosaccharides/α-glucosides, potentially derived from fructan, starch, or glycogen

name: Chitin and Related Oligosaccharides
notes: Genes associated with chitooligosaccharide processing and N-acetylhexosaminide hydrolysis; substrates may also derive from bacterial peptidoglycan and other glycoconjugates.

name: Other Oligosaccharides
notes: Mixed glycoside/oligosaccharide processing and AA7-associated carbohydrate oxidation activities with variable substrate specificity.

name: Cellobiose
notes: Glucose disaccharide produced during cellulose breakdown; utilization does not imply direct cellulose degradation.

name: Maltose
notes: Glucose disaccharide associated with starch and glycogen breakdown.

name: Sucrose
notes: Glucose-fructose disaccharide commonly found in plants; important for carbon transport and storage.

name: Trehalose
notes: Glucose disaccharide used for carbon storage and stress protection in many organisms.

name: Lactose
notes: Galactose-glucose disaccharide; utilization indicates potential to process lactose or related β-galactosides.

name: Mannose/Mannobiose (mixed size)
notes: Mannose-containing carbohydrates associated with mannan and other glycans; calls may represent monosaccharide or disaccharide processing.

name: Glucose
notes: Central hexose used in carbohydrate metabolism.

name: Xylose
notes: Pentose commonly derived from xylan and other plant polysaccharides.

name: Arabinose
notes: Pentose commonly found in plant cell-wall polysaccharides, including hemicellulose (e.g., arabinoxylan), arabinan, and pectin.

name: Mannose
notes: Hexose commonly found in plant cell-wall polysaccharides, including hemicellulose and pectin, as well as diverse glycoconjugates

name: Galactose
notes: Hexose found in plant cell-wall polysaccharides, including pectin (galactans) and some hemicelluloses, as well as other glycans.

name: Fructose
notes: Hexose found in sucrose and fructans (e.g., inulin and levan), as well as other carbohydrates.

name: Rhamnose
notes: Deoxyhexose commonly found in pectin (rhamnogalacturonans) and microbial polysaccharides.

name: N-Acetylglucosamine (Glc-NAc)
notes: Amino sugar found in chitin (fungal cell walls), bacterial peptidoglycan, and other glycoconjugates.

name: Fucose
notes: Deoxyhexose found in plant cell-wall polysaccharides, including xyloglucans and pectins, as well as microbial polysaccharides and diverse glycoconjugates.

name: CO2 Fixation
notes: Genes associated with autotrophic CO₂ fixation pathways; individual gene annotations do not necessarily indicate a complete pathway.

name: CH4 Oxidation Aerobic
notes: Particulate methane monooxygenase marker associated with aerobic methane oxidation; does not establish a complete methanotrophic pathway.

name: CH4 Production or Anaerobic Oxidation
notes: Methanogenesis-associated genes that may also occur in anaerobic methane-oxidizing archaea (ANME); gene presence alone does not distinguish methane production from oxidation.

name: Candidate Extracellular Aspartic Peptidases
notes: Hydrolyze peptide bonds in proteins using an aspartic acid catalytic mechanism. Selected MEROPS families include extracellular proteases; confirm cellular localization.

name: Candidate Extracellular Cysteine Peptidases
notes: Hydrolyze proteins and peptides using a cysteine catalytic mechanism. Selected families include extracellular and intracellular enzymes; confirm cellular localization.

name: Candidate Extracellular Glutamic Peptidases
notes: Hydrolyze proteins using a glutamic acid catalytic mechanism, including secreted fungal proteases. Confirm cellular localization.

name: Candidate Extracellular Metallo Peptidases
notes: Hydrolyze proteins and peptides using metal-dependent catalysis. Selected families include extracellular proteases; confirm cellular localization.

name: Candidate Extracellular Serine Peptidases
notes: Hydrolyze proteins and peptides using a serine catalytic mechanism. Selected families include secreted and intracellular proteases; confirm cellular localization.

name: Urease
notes: Hydrolyzes urea to ammonia and carbon dioxide, contributing directly to N mineralization. Can be intracellular, cell-associated, or extracellular; confirm cellular localization.

name: Amidase
notes: Hydrolyzes amides to release ammonia and corresponding organic acids, contributing to N mineralization. Often intracellular; confirm cellular localization.

name: Formamidase
notes: Hydrolyzes formamide to formate and ammonia, contributing to N mineralization. Typically intracellular; confirm cellular localization.

name: Organic Sulfur Mineralization
notes: Enzymatically transforms organic sulfur compounds, including sulfonates and sulfate esters, releasing inorganic sulfur (sulfite or sulfate) that can become available for microbial or plant uptake. Some enzymes may be intracellular or extracellular; confirm cellular localization.

name: Organic Phosphorus Mineralization
notes: Enzymatically hydrolyzes organic phosphorus compounds to release inorganic phosphate, contributing to phosphorus availability. Enzymes may be extracellular, cell-associated, or intracellular; confirm cellular localization.

name: Phytase
notes: Cleaves carbon-phosphorus bonds in phosphonates, releasing phosphate for microbial phosphorus acquisition. Typically functions intracellularly; confirm cellular localization.

name: IAA Biosynthesis - IAM
notes: K00466 is pathway-associated; K21801 is more specific than the broad amidase K01426. IAA production is not confirmed.

name: Cytokinin Biosynthesis Machinery
notes: cytokinin biosynthesis-associated adenylate isopentenyltransferases (K22871 or K10760), which catalyze the formation of cytokinin precursors. Indicates potential cytokinin production but does not confirm bioactive cytokinin synthesis or secretion.

name: Cytokinin Degradation
notes: cytokinin dehydrogenase, which degrades cytokinins and can regulate their availability. Indicates potential cytokinin degradation, not confirmed activity.

name: Gibberellin Biosynthetic Machinery
notes: bacterial gibberellin biosynthesis-associated P450 enzymes (CYP112, CYP114, CYP117). Suggests gibberellin biosynthetic potential but does not confirm a complete pathway or bioactive gibberellin production

name: ACC Modification (Deaminase)
notes: ACC deaminase (acdS), which converts 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC), the precursor of plant ethylene, into α-ketobutyrate and ammonia. May reduce plant ethylene production and alleviate stress responses. Indicates potential activity, not confirmed plant growth promotion.

name: Possible IAA Biosynthesis - IPyA
notes: IAA-associated decarboxylase (K04103) and nonspecific aldehyde dehydrogenase (K00128). Possible IAA production; interpret cautiously.

name: Possible IAA Biosynthesis - Tryptamine
notes: three broad-specificity enzymes that may support IAA synthesis through tryptamine. Weaker evidence for IAA production.

name: Possible IAA Biosynthesis - IAN
notes: Nonspecific nitrilase (K01501); single gene provides very weak evidence for IAA biosynthesis.

name: Arsenite Oxidation Potential
group: Other Metal and Trace Element Transformation and Resistance
notes: As(III) → As(V). Generally produces the less toxic form of inorganic arsenic, although mobility depends on soil conditions (sorption to iron)

name: Arsenate Reduction Potential
group: Other Metal and Trace Element Transformation and Resistance
notes: Converts As(V) to As(III), potentially increasing mobility and plant exposure; ArsC (K00537, K03741) mediates cellular detoxification and may not result in substantial environmental As(III) release.

name: Arsenic Methylation
group: Other Metal and Trace Element Transformation and Resistance
notes: Produces methylated arsenic species with variable toxicity, mobility, and plant uptake.

name: Mercury Reduction
group: Other Metal and Trace Element Transformation and Resistance
notes: MerA reduces Hg(II) to volatile Hg(0), affecting mercury mobility and atmospheric release.

name: Mercury Export
group: Other Metal and Trace Element Transformation and Resistance

name: Mercury Methylation
group: Other Metal and Trace Element Transformation and Resistance
notes: HgcA indicates potential for methylmercury production, increasing toxicity and bioaccumulation risk.

name: Organic Mercury Degradation
group: Other Metal and Trace Element Transformation and Resistance
notes: MerB cleaves organomercury compounds, including methylmercury, releasing Hg(II).

name: Copper Efflux
group: Other Metal and Trace Element Transformation and Resistance
notes: Detects microbial copper export systems associated with resistance to excess copper from fungicides, manure, and other agricultural inputs.

name: Zinc/Cadmium/Cobalt/Nickel Efflux
group: Other Metal and Trace Element Transformation and Resistance

name: Chromium/Silver Efflux
group: Other Metal and Trace Element Transformation and Resistance

name: Atrazine Degradation Pathway
notes: AtzA, AtzB, and AtzC catalyze sequential atrazine degradation to cyanuric acid. Does not indicate complete mineralization.

name: Initial 2,4-D Degradation
notes: TfdA, which initiates 2,4-D herbicide degradation to 2,4-dichlorophenol. Does not indicate complete degradation or mineralization

name: Initial Pyrethroid Degradation
notes: Pyrethroid hydrolase (PytH) cleaves ester bonds in pyrethroid insecticides. Indicates potential degradation, not complete mineralization.
